newsitem.title: CENTRAL AFRICAN REPUBLIC: Soldiers start mutiny in Central African Republic.
newsitem.headline: Soldiers start mutiny in Central African Republic.

text.p: Soldiers of the Central African Republic army launched a mutiny in the capital Bangui after forcibly taking weapons from the armoury, witnesses and military sources said on Saturday.

Witnesses said troops were moving from the eastern districts of the capital to the city centre where the presidential palace, the radio and television station and President Ange-Felix Patasse's residential villa are located.
"They broke into the armoury around midnight and stole arms and then firing broke out," a senior loyalist army officer told Reuters.

Another soldier in the main Kasai barracks outside the capital said by telephone that about 200 soldiers from the camp had gone to various parts of the city to try and disarm militiamen loyal to Patasse.
Loyalist presidential guard troops sealed off the deserted city centre, scene of serious clashes last May during a similar revolt which was put down by French troops.
France has a key military base in Central African Republic under defence accords between Paris and its former African colonies.

The Central Africa base has been key in France's long history of military intervention in Africa, including Rwanda where Paris is again preparing to send troops in a multinational mission to help war refugees.
Troops revolted for about four days from May 18 accusing Patasse of trying to disarm them. The mutiny ended after the president made some concessions.
